2) $$\frac{\cos A - \sin A}{\cos A + \sin A} = \frac{1 - \sqrt{3}}{1 + \sqrt{3}}$$

or, $$\frac{\cos A - \sin A + \cos A + \sin A}{\cos A - \sin A - \cos A - \sin A} = \frac{1 - \sqrt{3} + 1 + \sqrt{3}}{1 - \sqrt{3} - 1 - \sqrt{3}}$$ [By addition-subtraction]

or, $$\frac{2\cos A}{-2\sin A} = \frac{2}{-2\sqrt{3}}$$

or, $$\frac{\cos A}{\sin A} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$

or, $$\cot A = \cot 60^\circ$$

$$\therefore A = 60^\circ$$

3) Given that, $$A = 45^\circ$$

we have to prove that, $$\cos 2A = \frac{1 - \tan^2 A}{1 + \tan^2 A}$$

L.H.S. = $$\cos 2A$$

= $$\cos(2 \times 45^\circ) = \cos 90^\circ = 0$$

R.H.S. = $$\frac{1 - \tan^2 A}{1 + \tan^2 A}$$

= $$\frac{1 - \tan^2 45^\circ}{1 + \tan^2 45^\circ} = \frac{1 - (1)^2}{1 + (1)^2}$$

= $$\frac{0}{2} = 0$$

$$\therefore$$ L.H.S. = R.H.S. (Proved)
